title: CRLR/133/2009 of ASRAR SIDDIQUI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 133 of 2009
Asrar Siddiqui ....... Revisionist
 versus
State of Uttarakhand ....... Respondent
Mr. K.S. Verma, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. V.K. Gemini, Dy. Advocate General with Mr. V.S. Rathore,
Brief Holder for the respondent State.
U.C. Dhyani, J.(Oral) Learned counsel for the revisionist confined his
prayer only to the extent that the revisionist be directed to
be sentenced for the period already undergone by him
alongwith payment of fine. Revisionist was convicted for
the offences punishable under Sections 409, 420, 467, 471
IPC. He was directed to undergo simple imprisonment for
three years for each offence punishable under Sections 409,
467 and 471 IPC. He was also directed to undergo simple
imprisonment for two years in connection with each
offence punishable under Section 420 and 468 IPC. All the
sentences were directed to run concurrently.
2) The accused was also directed to pay a fine of
Rs. 20,000/- on first three counts each and a fine of Rs.
10,000/- on subsequent two counts each. He was directed
to pay fine of Rs. 20,000/- each under Sections 409, 467
and 471 IPC, failing which he was to undergo further
simple imprisonment for three months on each count. He
was also directed to pay fine of Rs. 10,000/- each under
Sections 420, 468 IPC, failing which he was to undergo
further simple imprisonment for two months on each count.

3) It is the submission of learned counsel for the
revisionist that revisionist remained in jail for one year
eight months and is ready to deposit the amount of fine
imposed upon him. Revisionist had already attained the
age of superannuation and the FIR was lodged after three
years of his retirement. He was a Head Clerk in the office
of District Commandant Home Guards, Haridwar.
4) After hearing learned counsel for the
revisionist, learned Dy. Advocate General and having gone
through the record of the case, conviction of the revisionist
for the aforementioned offences is maintained. Criminal
revision is, therefore, dismissed summarily so far as the
conviction of the revisionist for the offences alleged against
him is concerned.
5) Considering the fact that the revisionist
remained in jail for one year eight months, as against his
sentence for three years, coupled with the fact that the
revisionist had already attained superannuation when the
FIR was lodged against him after three years of his
superannuation, as also the fact that he is ready to deposit
the amount of fine imposed upon him by the trial court, as
affirmed by the lower appellate court, the money
embezzled has already been restored to the State
exchequer, this court deems it fit, despite the gravity of
offence, to direct that the revisionist shall be sentenced for
the period already undergone by him (i.e. one year eight
months imprisonment) alongwith fine, which was imposed
upon him by the trial court. The amount of fine which has

already been deposited before the trial court shall be
adjusted in the amount of fine.
6) The revisionist is, therefore, directed to deposit
fine of Rs. 20,000/- in connection with offence punishable
under Section 409 IPC; fine of Rs. 20,000/- in relation to
the offence punishable under Section 467 IPC; fine of Rs.
20,000/- under Section 471 IPC; fine of Rs. 10,000/- in
relation to the offence punishable under Section 420 IPC
and fine of Rs. 10,000/- in connection with offence
punishable under Section 468 IPC, within a period of one
month from today, failing which the trial court shall be at
liberty to take necessary measures for sending the
revisionist to jail, in default of payment of fine, for the
period directed by it and affirmed by lower appellate court.
7) With the directions as above, the criminal
revision is finally disposed of.
8) Let a copy of this judgment alongwith lower
court records be sent to the court concerned for ensuring
compliance.
